relationships.description: Connects DDD Strategic Context Mapping to system design hld architectures in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Defining Bounded Context perimeters, Ubiquitous Language boundaries, and explicit integration patterns (ACL, OHS, Published Language) across teams.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Strategic DDD—from why shared enterprise models break down to choosing ACL vs Conformist vs Open Host Service.

spark.summary: Explicitly defining bounded contexts, their ubiquitous language boundaries, and the upstream/downstream integration relationships between teams and services in a complex domain.
spark.keyTakeaway: A single enterprise-wide canonical data model breaks down across teams; explicit context maps protect each model's integrity with intentional translation boundaries.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A `Customer` in Sales (lead score, pipeline stage) is fundamentally different from a `Customer` in Billing (tax ID, credit limit) or Shipping (geo-coordinates).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Checkout (OHS) -> Fulfillment -> Legacy ERP (ACL) Integration (Checkout (Core) -> Published Event -> Fulfillment -> ERP ACL Adapter -> Legacy ERP); Autonomous Contexts Communicating via Published Language & ACLs (Checkout Context -> Fulfillment Context -> Billing Context -> Schema Registry).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Pick the integration pattern that matches the upstream/downstream power dynamic and semantic alignment. Prohibit cross-context database joins: each Bounded Context owns its tables and migrations, communicates via OHS APIs or Schema-Registry-verified events, and reserves full ACLs.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect strategic context mapping with tactical DDD aggregates, event schema evolution, and Data Mesh product boundaries.

learningJourney.title: What are Bounded Contexts & Strategic Context Mapping
learningJourney.explanation:
A `Customer` in Sales (lead score, pipeline stage) is fundamentally different from a `Customer` in Billing (tax ID, credit limit) or Shipping (geo-coordinates). Forcing all three into one class creates a brittle **Big Ball of Mud**.

A **Bounded Context** defines the explicit perimeter within which a specific **Ubiquitous Language** and domain model apply. **Context Mapping** documents how contexts integrate—technically (APIs, events, translators) and organizationally (Conway's Law)—using patterns like **Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)**, **Open Host Service (OHS) + Published Language**, **Customer-Supplier**, **Conformist**, and **Shared Kernel**.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Bounded Contexts & Strategic Context Mapping works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Shared Schemas Break Teams (and How ACL + OHS Isolate Churn)
learningJourney.explanation: Sharing one monolithic `Order` or `Customer` database table across 4+ teams creates semantic drift: Sales changes `Account.status = 'ACTIVE'` to include trial users, silently causing Billing to invoice free accounts. Explicit OHS/Published Language contracts upstream and ACL translators downstream isolate each context's internal model.

sectionDiagram.title: Checkout (OHS) -> Fulfillment -> Legacy ERP (ACL) Integration
sectionDiagram.summary: Published Language decouples Checkout from N consumers, while the ACL insulates Fulfillment from cryptic legacy ERP schemas.

ideas.title: Insulating Pricing from a Legacy ERP via ACL
ideas.description: A 15-year-old ERP exposed cryptic `STAT_X9` XML payloads. An ACL adapter mapped them into `TaxJurisdiction` and `WholesaleCost` value objects, isolating ERP churn to one translator module.

ideas.title: Orders Open Host Service for 4 Downstream Teams
ideas.description: Instead of building bespoke REST fields for Warehouse, Fraud, Notifications, and Data Lake, Orders published a versioned Kafka `OrderPlaced` Avro/Protobuf contract via Schema Registry.

learningJourney.title: Where Strategic Context Mapping Applies
learningJourney.explanation: Use Context Mapping when multiple teams share domain nouns with divergent meanings or integrate with volatile external/legacy systems.

benefits: Prevents cross-team deployment freezes and insulates core domains from vendor DTO leakage.
costs: ACL translation layers add mapping boilerplate and contract tests.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Small 1–2 Team CRUD Apps / Shifting Prototypes
benefits: A single shared relational schema is far faster when boundaries are still fluid.
costs: Premature context splitting creates chatty RPCs and distributed joins.

benefits: Group contexts by cohesive business capabilities, not individual DB tables.
costs: Table-per-service splits turn simple queries into distributed RPC chains.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Enforce Boundaries in Modular Monoliths & Event Schemas
learningJourney.explanation: Bounded Contexts do **not** require separate microservices on day one. Tools like **Spring Modulith** or **ArchUnit** enforce context boundaries inside a single deployable binary—blocking direct repository imports across packages while allowing in-process domain events. For async Published Language, enforce `BACKWARD` / `FULL` compatibility in Schema Registry / Buf.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Comparing the 5 Core Context Mapping Patterns
learningJourney.explanation: Pick the integration pattern that matches the upstream/downstream power dynamic and semantic alignment.

benefits: Low coupling; protects core domain from messy legacy/vendor DTOs.
costs: Extra translator boilerplate and mapping tests at the edge.

benefits: Scales cleanly to N downstream consumers via versioned OpenAPI/Protobuf/Avro.
costs: Requires Schema Registry governance and deprecation SLAs.

benefits: Downstream team negotiates needed fields with an aligned internal upstream team.
costs: Requires Pact contract tests and shared sprint prioritization.

benefits: Zero translation (Conformist) or zero duplication of core primitives (Shared Kernel).
costs: Conformist leaks upstream changes; Shared Kernel couples CI/CD pipelines.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: Context Boundary & Event Governance
learningJourney.explanation: Prohibit cross-context database joins: each Bounded Context owns its tables and migrations, communicates via OHS APIs or Schema-Registry-verified events, and reserves full ACLs for volatile/legacy boundaries (avoiding over-engineered DTO mappers between two clean internal Customer-Supplier services).

sectionDiagram.title: Autonomous Contexts Communicating via Published Language & ACLs
sectionDiagram.summary: Each Bounded Context owns its private database schema and integrates strictly through versioned contracts or ACLs.

knowledgeCheck.question: A core Pricing service integrates with a 15-year-old ERP exposing cryptic `STAT_X9` XML codes. The Pricing team imports the ERP's generated XML classes directly into its core pricing domain entities. What anti-pattern is this, and how should it be fixed?

options.text: Unintended Conformist (leaky upstream model); wrap the ERP client in an Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) at the edge that translates XML into domain-native Value Objects
options.feedback: Correct: an ACL insulates the core domain from legacy ERP churn and cryptic semantics.

options.text: Shared Kernel; merge both databases into one shared schema
options.feedback: Sharing a database creates a Big Ball of Mud with multi-team migration freezes.

options.text: Separate Ways; stop integrating with the ERP
options.feedback: Pricing genuinely needs ERP base costs, so integration via an ACL is required.

_recommendedProblem.prompt: Design a payment and ledger system (like Stripe or PayPal) processing 5,000 TPS where no dollar can ever be double-charged, lost, or created out of thin air—even across network retries and PSP timeouts.
